items.q: It was so dark in the clinic corridor that I had to ______ at the sign to read the doctor's name.
items.vi: Hành lang phòng khám tối đến nỗi tôi phải nheo mắt nhìn kỹ tấm biển mới đọc được tên bác sĩ.
items.explanation: Word choice: peer at = look closely and with difficulty, which fits so dark and having to read the sign. ✗ glimpse — see briefly by chance, and takes a direct object, not at; ✗ notice — become aware of something, no effort, no at; ✗ observe — watch carefully for a long time, takes a direct object, not at.

items.q: Can you ______ any spelling mistakes in my post before I upload it?
items.vi: Bạn có thể phát hiện lỗi chính tả nào trong bài đăng của mình trước khi mình tải lên không?
items.explanation: Word choice: spot = notice something that is hard to find, and it takes a direct object — spot any spelling mistakes. ✗ glance — take a quick look, needs at; ✗ stare — look fixedly, needs at; ✗ gaze — look steadily in admiration or wonder, needs at. None of the three can take 'mistakes' as its object.

items.q: The little boy ______ at the goldfish in the doctor's waiting room for almost an hour.
items.vi: Cậu bé ngắm nhìn đàn cá vàng trong phòng chờ của bác sĩ gần cả tiếng đồng hồ.
items.explanation: Word choice: gaze at = look steadily for a long time, which matches for almost an hour and the preposition at. ✗ glimpsed — saw for a moment, takes a direct object; ✗ spotted — noticed suddenly, takes a direct object; ✗ noticed — became aware of, takes a direct object. All three are momentary and never take at.

items.q: I only caught a ______ of the famous striker before the crowd closed in around him.
items.vi: Tôi chỉ kịp thoáng thấy cầu thủ tiền đạo nổi tiếng trước khi đám đông vây quanh anh ấy.
items.explanation: Fixed expression: catch a glimpse of = see something for a very short time, which fits only ... before the crowd closed in. ✗ glance — a quick look you take or cast, not catch; ✗ view — what you can see from a place, used with have/get a view of; ✗ stare — a long fixed look, used with give a stare, not catch.

items.q: Lan spent the whole evening ______ the internet for a second-hand bicycle.
items.vi: Lan dành cả buổi tối lướt mạng để tìm một chiếc xe đạp cũ.
items.explanation: Word choice: browse the internet = look through websites without a fixed plan, which fits the whole evening ... for a bicycle; browse takes a direct object. ✗ peeking — take a quick secret look, needs at; ✗ glancing — take a quick look, needs at; ✗ staring — look fixedly, needs at. All three describe one short look, not searching online.

items.q: Please ______ attention to the road signs when you cycle through the city centre.
items.vi: Hãy chú ý các biển báo giao thông khi bạn đạp xe qua trung tâm thành phố.
items.explanation: Collocation: the fixed verb with attention is pay attention to. ✗ take — take care / take notice, but never take attention; ✗ make — make an effort / make a note, not attention; ✗ put — put effort into, not attention. Only pay collocates with this noun.

items.q: When the teacher asked who had broken the window, Nam decided to ______ the truth.
items.vi: Khi cô giáo hỏi ai đã làm vỡ cửa sổ, Nam quyết định nói thật.
items.explanation: Collocation: the fixed verb with the truth is tell the truth (like tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke). ✗ say — reports the actual words spoken (say 'sorry'), not truth or lies; ✗ speak — a language or in a way (speak English, speak loudly), no object 'the truth'; ✗ talk — is intransitive: talk about / talk to, never talk the truth.

items.q: My grandfather cycles ten kilometres every morning to ______ fit.
items.vi: Ông tôi đạp xe mười ki-lô-mét mỗi sáng để giữ gìn sức khỏe.
items.explanation: Collocation: the verb before fit (= healthy through exercise) is keep fit or stay fit, and cycles every morning shows a continuing habit. ✗ hold — hold means grip or contain, never used before an adjective like fit; ✗ make — make + adjective needs an object (make him fit), and here there is none; ✗ go — go + adjective is for changes like go bad / go grey, not fit.

items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Minh: He ______ badminton at the sports centre. He'll be home by six.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Minh: Cậu ấy đang chơi cầu lông ở trung tâm thể thao. Sáu giờ cậu ấy sẽ về.
items.explanation: Tense: an action in progress at the moment of speaking (Where's Nam? ... He'll be home by six) takes the present continuous: is playing. ✗ plays — present simple is for habits (plays every Friday), not what he is doing now; ✗ has played — present perfect means the game is over, but he is still out; ✗ played — past simple is a finished action, not something happening now.

items.q: I ______ this phone for three years, and the battery still lasts all day.
items.vi: Tôi đã dùng chiếc điện thoại này ba năm rồi mà pin vẫn dùng được cả ngày.
items.explanation: Tense: for three years with a situation that still continues (the battery still lasts) takes the present perfect: have had. ✗ had — past simple would mean I no longer have the phone; ✗ am having — have meaning 'possess' is a state verb and is not used in the continuous; ✗ have — present simple cannot combine with a for + duration stretching back into the past.

items.q: Lan: Are you free on Sunday? / Nam: No, I ______ my cousin in Da Lat. We booked the bus tickets last week.
items.vi: Lan: Chủ nhật bạn có rảnh không? / Nam: Không, mình đi thăm anh họ ở Đà Lạt. Bọn mình đặt vé xe từ tuần trước rồi.
items.explanation: Tense: a personal arrangement already fixed for the future (We booked the bus tickets last week) takes the present continuous: am visiting on Sunday. ✗ visit — present simple is for timetables (the bus leaves at six), not personal plans; ✗ visited — past simple describes a finished visit, but Sunday is still to come; ✗ have visited — present perfect means the visit has already happened.

items.q: Mai was ______ when she found out she had won the chess tournament.
items.vi: Mai vui sướng tột độ khi biết mình đã thắng giải cờ vua.
items.explanation: Idiom: over the moon = extremely happy, which fits she had won the tournament. ✗ under the weather — slightly ill; ✗ on the fence — undecided between two choices; ✗ in the dark — not told about something. None of the three describes joy at winning.

items.q: After months of talking about it, my brother finally ______ and signed up for the marathon.
items.vi: Sau nhiều tháng chỉ nói suông, cuối cùng anh tôi cũng quyết tâm dấn thân và đăng ký chạy marathon.
items.explanation: Idiom: take the plunge = finally do something big or risky after hesitating, which fits after months of talking about it ... finally. ✗ took the biscuit — was the most annoying or surprising of all; ✗ took the floor — began to speak in a meeting; ✗ took the hint — understood an indirect message. Only the plunge fits signing up for a marathon.

items.q: Don't ______ our team just because we lost the first two matches of the season.
items.vi: Đừng vội coi đội mình là vô vọng chỉ vì thua hai trận đầu mùa giải.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: write off = decide that someone or something is a failure and give up on them, which fits just because we lost the first two matches. ✗ write down — note on paper; ✗ write up — turn notes into a full report; ✗ write out — write in full, without abbreviations. A team cannot be noted, reported or written in full.

items.q: Nam refused to ______ in the argument about which phone is better, even when he was clearly wrong.
items.vi: Nam nhất quyết không chịu nhượng bộ trong cuộc tranh cãi xem điện thoại nào tốt hơn, dù cậu ấy rõ ràng đã sai.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: back down = admit you are wrong and stop arguing, which fits refused to ... in the argument ... even when he was clearly wrong. ✗ back up — support someone, or copy computer data; ✗ back out — withdraw from a promise or agreement; ✗ back away — move backwards physically, away from danger.

items.q: Lan: Nam isn't answering his phone. / Mai: He ______ be at the doctor's; he said he had an appointment at nine.
items.vi: Lan: Nam không nghe điện thoại. / Mai: Chắc chắn cậu ấy đang ở chỗ bác sĩ; cậu ấy nói có hẹn lúc chín giờ.
items.explanation: Modal of deduction: must = the speaker is almost sure it is true, and the evidence is given — he said he had an appointment at nine. ✗ can't — deduction that it is impossible, the opposite of the evidence; ✗ needn't — no obligation to do something, not a guess about where he is; ✗ mustn't — prohibition (not allowed), never used for deduction.

items.q: The doctor ______ treated my grandmother has just opened a clinic near our school.
items.vi: Vị bác sĩ đã chữa bệnh cho bà tôi vừa mở một phòng khám gần trường chúng tôi.
items.explanation: Relative pronoun: the gap is the subject of treated and refers to a person (the doctor), so who is needed. ✗ whom — object form only (the doctor whom we saw); here the verb has no other subject; ✗ whose — possessive, must be followed by a noun (whose clinic); ✗ which — for things and animals, not people.

items.q: Only ______ people in my class still use a phone without internet access.
items.vi: Chỉ một vài bạn trong lớp tôi còn dùng điện thoại không có kết nối mạng.
items.explanation: Quantifier: people is a plural countable noun, so it takes a few (= a small number). ✗ a little — only with uncountable nouns (a little time); ✗ much — only with uncountable nouns, and used mainly in negatives and questions; ✗ little — uncountable only, and would mean 'almost none', not a small group that still exists.

items.q: Remember ______ your phone before the exam starts, or the teacher will take it away.
items.vi: Nhớ tắt điện thoại trước khi bài thi bắt đầu, nếu không cô giáo sẽ thu đấy.
items.explanation: Gerund vs infinitive: remember to do = don't forget a duty still to be done, and before the exam starts shows the action is still ahead. ✗ switching off — remember doing = recall a memory of something already done; ✗ switch off — a bare infinitive never follows remember; ✗ to switching off — to + gerund is not a possible form after remember.

items.q: Mai forgot to water the plants on the balcony for two weeks; ______, most of them died.
items.vi: Mai quên tưới cây trên ban công suốt hai tuần; kết quả là phần lớn cây đều chết.
items.explanation: Linking word: the second clause is the consequence of forgetting to water the plants, so as a result is needed. ✗ even so — contrast (despite that), but the plants dying is not surprising; ✗ in addition — adds a similar point, not an effect; ✗ on the contrary — denies the previous statement and says the opposite.

items.q: If my dad hadn't bailed me out, I ______ my phone bill last month.
items.vi: Nếu bố không giúp tôi thoát khỏi cảnh túng thiếu, tháng trước tôi đã không thể trả nổi tiền cước điện thoại.
items.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect (hadn't bailed) and last month mark an unreal past, so the result clause needs could have + past participle: couldn't have paid. ✗ couldn't pay — second conditional, for an unreal present, not last month; ✗ can't pay — present ability, cannot follow a past-perfect if-clause; ✗ won't pay — first conditional, a real future, not an imagined past.

items.q: Neither the coach nor the players ______ happy with the referee's decision.
items.vi: Cả huấn luyện viên lẫn các cầu thủ đều không hài lòng với quyết định của trọng tài.
items.explanation: Agreement: with neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the players (plural), so were is correct; the referee's decision sets the sentence in the past. ✗ was — singular, agrees with 'the coach', the farther subject; ✗ is — singular and present; ✗ has been — singular and present perfect, wrong number and wrong time.

items.q: ______ by a virus from a free download site, my laptop stopped working completely.
items.vi: Bị nhiễm vi-rút từ một trang tải miễn phí, máy tính xách tay của tôi ngừng hoạt động hoàn toàn.
items.explanation: Participle clause: the laptop was infected by the virus (it did not infect anything), and by a virus signals a passive, so a past participle opens the clause: Infected by. ✗ Infecting — active, would make the laptop the one infecting; ✗ Having infected — active perfect participle, same problem; ✗ To infect — an infinitive of purpose, and the laptop had no purpose to infect.

items.q: ______ finishes the crossword first will get a free ice cream from Dad.
items.vi: Ai giải xong ô chữ trước sẽ được bố thưởng một cây kem miễn phí.
items.explanation: Pronoun: the gap is the subject of finishes, and whoever = 'the person who' does that job. ✗ Whomever — object form, cannot be the subject of a verb; ✗ Whom — object form and a question/relative word, not 'the person who'; ✗ Whose — possessive, needs a noun after it (whose crossword).

items.q: You haven't been to the dentist for two years, ______?
items.vi: Hai năm nay bạn chưa đi khám nha sĩ, đúng không?
items.explanation: Question tag: the statement is negative present perfect (haven't been), so the tag is positive with the same auxiliary: have you. ✗ haven't you — negative tag after a negative statement; tags flip; ✗ did you — the auxiliary must match; the statement uses have, not did; ✗ do you — wrong auxiliary; do is only for present simple.
